title: The printing press ↔ ideas going viral

learning.goal: Understand how cheap, identical printed copies let ideas spread faster than anyone could stop them, and how that reshaped religion, science and reading in Europe between 1440 and 1600.
learning.question: The internet also made copying almost free. Which change after 1440 does it most resemble, and what is different?
learning.answer: One grounded reading: like the press, it lets one voice reach many people fast. Luther used short, cheap pamphlets much as people use posts today. A difference: printing still needed a press, paper and a printer willing to risk censorship, so there were still gatekeepers.
learning.caveat: Simplified: movable type existed earlier in China and Korea; Gutenberg's press in Mainz (c. 1440–1455) combined metal type, oil-based ink and a screw press. The press worked together with other forces (trade, the Renaissance, church and state politics). Figures such as 250+ printing towns by 1500 and book totals are historians' estimates.

steps.text: How did one machine change Europe?
steps.say: Before 1440, a new idea spread only as fast as someone could copy it by hand.

steps.text: 1440–1600: from hand-copied books to a continent of print
a year or more per Bible

steps.say: Around 1450, Gutenberg's press in Mainz printed in weeks what took a scribe years.
The secret was small metal letters that could be arranged, printed, and used again.

steps.text: ink it, press paper, peel off a page

steps.say: Every copy came out the same, and the letters went on to the next page.
In fifty years, presses spread to hundreds of towns across Europe.

steps.title: Religion
steps.say: Luther's cheap pamphlets reached all of Germany in weeks. The Church could not burn them fast enough.

steps.title: Science
steps.say: Scholars far apart read identical copies, compared them, and corrected each other.

steps.title: Readers
steps.say: Books got cheaper and appeared in German, English, French — not only Latin.

steps.text: Ideas became copyable, cheap, and hard to erase.
steps.say: The press did not cause all this alone, but it made ideas copyable, cheap, and hard to erase.
